other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: India stands with the countries having the fastest growth rate, recording a 5% CAGR, driven by rapid economic expansion and rising middle-class consumption.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Global private final consumption expenditure (PFCE) has witnessed steady growth, reaching USD 63 trillion in CY 2024, up from USD 49 trillion in CY 2019, reflecting a CAGR of 5%.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The United States leads in absolute PFCE, reaching USD 19.9 trillion in CY 2024 with a 7% CAGR, underscoring its consumer- driven economy.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: However, the market is projected to slow down and increase at a CAGR of 3%-4% to reach USD 2,165-2,275 billion by CY 2030, as macroeconomic headwinds weigh on discretionary spending and earlier price-driven growth makes volume-led momentum harder to sustain.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Figure 2-1: India’s real GDP (₹ trillion) and GDP growth (%), in FY Source: RBI, 1Lattice analysis 2.2 Increasing Per-capita Income India’s per capita gross national income (GNI) has seen strong growth in recent years, reaching ₹ 2,47,487 in FY 2026, from ₹ 1,40,899 in FY 2019, reflecting a CAGR of 8.4%.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
